title: Clean emission of a polynomial-time function
statement: Every polynomial-time computable function $f$ on binary words has a finite Turing machine $M$, natural numbers $A,d$, and a clean computation such that for every binary input $x$ and argument word, the computation first halts at a positive time no greater than $A(n+1)^d$, where $n$ is the argument length; at that time its tape words encode the unchanged argument and its output is exactly $f$ of the argument.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a polynomial-time computable function on binary words
replaced: Every polynomial-time computable string function $f$ has a first-halting clean module that preserves the argument word, emits exactly $f$ of the argument as output, and runs within a polynomial budget of the argument length, including cleanup and the final halt.
